title: Conformance report
description: A dated conformance report, per SPEC.md §7. NOT a protocol document: it is emitted by the harness, never by a Server, and its member names are deliberately absent from schemas/member-manifest.json — dragging them into Lock 2's set-equality check would break prove_member_manifest.sh for reasons nobody would find quickly. Reports are never restated (V8): a later run is a NEW report, keyed on (spec_version, register_version) with run_at making each entry of that series distinct. There is no field for a name, email, phone number, loyalty number or payment instrument, and no member that settles, authorises, captures, refunds or prices.

report_schema.description: The version of THIS document's own shape. Separate from spec_version, because the report format and the protocol version each move for their own reasons.

spec_version.description: The CHANGEOVER specification version the run asserted against. Half of V8's key.

register_version.description: The presentation-class register version. The other half of V8's key. A spec change does not invalidate an old report; it makes it an old report.

implementation.description: What was under test. Never a claim of affiliation with any vendor; a name a reader can check.

origin.description: Where the implementation was reached, when it was reached over a network. Absent for an in-process run.

bindings.description: The bindings this run was asked to exercise.

binding_coverage.description: One entry per requested binding, saying whether any class actually drove it. A binding nobody exercised is NOT a pass: the report may not claim conformance over a transport it never spoke.

classes.description: The classes that drove this binding. Empty exactly when exercised is false.

reason.description: REQUIRED when exercised is false. Why no class drove it, in terms that stay true.

run_at.description: RFC 3339 with a mandatory offset, read from the machine that ran the harness. The third element of the non-restatement key.

trials.description: Hold attempts made across the whole run. §7 names it because a concurrency result without one is not reproducible.

selection.description: Which classes this run was restricted to. A restricted run cannot produce a pass for a class it did not execute — every unselected class is unprovable, naming the restriction.

classes.description: One entry per §7 class. Every registered class appears, whether or not it could be reached: a class absent from the list is indistinguishable from a class that passed.

floor_violations.description: Holds that stopped holding inside their own floor with no revocation_reason. Counted at the boundary, scoped to this run's own principals.

operator_overrides.description: The same shape of event WITH a revocation_reason. Reported separately, because an honest exhibitor withdrawing seats must not read as non-conforming.

release_latency_ms.description: Release → the seat is somebody else's, measured across the boundary. Carries its substrate, so a report cannot quietly attribute an in-process number to an exhibitor.

oversell_events.description: Physical seats carrying more than one occupying row. The number this whole protocol exists to keep at zero.

harness.description: What produced the report. The commit hash is the whole point: a number without the code that measured it is an anecdote.

commit.description: The harness commit hash, or null where the tree is not a repository. Never a guess.

dirty.description: True when the working tree carried uncommitted changes. A dirty report says so rather than implying its commit is the code that ran.

concurrent.description: Whether the store could genuinely race two callers. False makes every concurrency class unprovable, and says why in one member.

unprovable.description: First-class, and never folded into either neighbour. A runner that collapses "we could not reach your server" into pass or fail destroys the only property that makes these reports worth publishing.

exit_code.description: 0 all-pass · 1 any-fail · 2 any-unprovable-and-no-fail. The third outcome has its own code because two codes cannot carry three answers.

binding.description: in_process is a real binding and is named as one: a class that drove the verbs directly spoke no transport, and calling that "http" would be a claim about a wire nobody put a byte on.

status.description: Three outcomes, not two. "Your server violated the floor" and "we could not reach your server" are different sentences and the report keeps them apart.

measured_by.description: The class or procedure the number came from. A number with no source is not evidence.

substrate.description: The driver and the scenario the samples came from. An in-process number and a number off a real boundary are not the same measurement and must not read as one.

spec_row.description: §7's own words for this row, carried so the report is auditable against the source rather than against a summary of it.

reason.description: REQUIRED on fail and on unprovable; forbidden on pass. An unreachable class with no stated reason is a place to put work.

missing_path.description: A repository path whose absence is the reason. Re-checked by the proof: the day the path appears, the blocker is stale and the suite says so.

source.description: The module that ran the class, repository-relative. Absent exactly when nothing ran it.

clauses.description: A §7 row is several clauses, and reporting a row as one boolean throws away which half was reached. Empty exactly when nothing ran — which is a fail or an unprovable, never a pass.
